channel.title: Religion News Service - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Religion News Service (religionnews.com)

item.title: Syrian Kurds return home to celebrate Nowruz for the first time since exile
item.description: AL BASOUTA, Syria (AP) — Nowruz, the Farsi-language word for “new year,” is an ancient Persian festival that is also celebrated by Kurds in Syria, Turkey and Iraq as well as Iran.

item.title: Supreme Court revives suit from evangelical Christian challenging restrictions on demonstrations
item.description: WASHINGTON (AP) —The high court unanimously ruled in the case of Gabriel Olivier, who says his religious and free speech rights were violated when he was arrested for refusing to move his preaching away from a suburban amphitheater.

item.title: Iranians mark Persian new year with heavy hearts as war cuts contact with loved ones
item.description: PARIS (AP) — An Iranian cultural center in Paris that organizes music events for Nowruz says it's in mourning. In the United States, some Iranian American communities also canceled or scaled back festivities.

item.title: Federal judge grants injunction allowing clergy visits at Minneapolis ICE holding facility
item.description: ST. PAUL, Minn. (AP) — U.S. District Judge Jerry Blackwell granted an injunction requested by Minnesota branches of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America, the United Church of Christ, and a Catholic priest who had sued the Department of Homeland Security.

item.title: Jehovah’s Witnesses ease policy on transfusions, allowing storage and use of one’s own blood
item.description: (AP) — The Governing Body of Jehovah’s Witnesses announced what it called a “clarification” of its teaching on Friday, saying it came after extensive prayer and consideration.

item.title: New book aims to break silence on Mormon temple garments
item.description: (RNS) — Two hundred women said they had medical obstacles to wearing LDS temple garments, according to a survey conducted for 'Mormon Garments: Sacred and Secret,' released last month.

item.title: Leighton Ford Ministries launches ‘LiveCalled’ to help leaders discern true calling
How a network of ordained women got Sarah Mullally to Canterbury
item.description: (RNS) — Mullally’s sometimes twisting journey to Canterbury may never have been completed if it hadn’t been for an Anglican organization called Leading Women.

item.title: Jerusalem's Palm Sunday procession canceled due to Iran war
item.description: JERUSALEM (RNS) — In lieu of the Palm Sunday procession, the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem called on Christians around the world to commit to a moment of prayer for the Holy City of Jerusalem.

item.title: How the sanctuary movement became the faithful's answer to ICE raids
item.description: (RNS) — The sanctuary movement has deep biblical roots, but it has evolved from the 1980s in important ways.

item.title: People 'bathe' in nature to get respite from chaotic news cycle
item.description: RALEIGH, N.C. (AP) — Based on the Japanese wellness practice of Shinrin-yoku, the activity has been known to reduce stress, improve mood, lower blood pressure and boost the immune system.

item.title: Trump says Iran is eager for a deal to end the war as he extends deadline to allow for diplomacy
item.description: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates (AP) — Trump’s turnaround, which held out the possibility of resolving the war now in its fourth week, served to drive down oil prices and jolt stocks.

item.title: UK police probe possible Iran link after Jewish charity ambulances set on fire
item.description: LONDON (AP) — Religious and political leaders condemned what Prime Minister Keir Starmer called a “horrific" attack.

item.title: Cardinal Robert McElroy explained best why the Iran war is immoral
item.description: (RNS) — That our adversaries use unjust means does not justify our doing the same.
